newsitem.title: USA: Safeway sees smooth transaction with Vons.
newsitem.headline: Safeway sees smooth transaction with Vons.

text.p: Safeway Inc chief executive officer of Steven Burd said he anticipates a "smooth transaction" with Vons Cos Inc.
"We expect we'll ultimately get a good reaction," Burd said on a conference call.

"We just started this process and none of us is exactly sure how long it will take to effect this transaction. We think its reasonable to think this could be completed in either the late first quarter or approximately sometime in the second quarter," he said. Vons earlier said it will study the $58 per share offer made by Safway and respond in due course.
Burd said Safeway did not think the transaction would have a significant effect on earnings per share in 1997.
"We expect this to enhance earnings per share beginning with the first full year of operations, which should be 1998, and we expect it to enhance earnings per share each year thereafter," he said.
Burd said he did not expect the merger would be disruptive to store employees or customers.
"We have virtually no overlap with Vons at this time and so there are no redundant facilities to worry about having to close," he said.
"The combination will produce more than Vons can produce on its own for shareholders at an accelerated pace," he said.

Safeway, which already owns 34.5 percent of Vons' outstanding shares, also has several representatives on Vons board. But a Safeway spokesman said the first time that Vons was approached about the proposed transaction was in a letter that was made public Wednesday.
Safeway said Safeway's total debt level is in the region of $1.8 billion. Vons' debt level is in the region of $600 million.

Terms of the deal calls for Safeway to issue 1.34 Safeway shares for each of the Vons shares not currently owned by Safeway. The deal values Vons at about $3.25 billion, including outstanding indebtedness.
